about: measure contests of 2022 in Nebraska, in the layout of plan/PLAN.md section 3 with the fields data/README.md adds (D3). Built by pipeline/local_medsl.py from pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py's cache.

medsl.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, Precinct-Level Returns 2022 by Individual State, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/UYQIEP, version 5.0
medsl.note: precinct returns compiled by MEDSL from each state's official sources (named per state in its README); added up to the contest by pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py, files ne22_cleaned.csv

model.name: the model's own forecast, method D3-v1.1
model.note: each year forecast from a fit on earlier years only; no polls are used

nara.name: National Archives, Electoral College Results (the sitting president's party)
nara.licence: US federal public record; no licence printed

klarner.name: Carl Klarner, State Legislative Election Returns, 1967-2022, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/FJOGJB, v1.0, released 2024-06-12T21:56:14Z (the races route (a) is fitted on)

question.title: Shall Judge Michael G Heavican Be Retained In Office? - 6 Year Term

threshold.rule: constitution leaves the manner to the Legislature; statute: majority of electors voting on the question retains
threshold.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. sec. 24-817 (authorized by Neb. Const. art. V, sec. 21(3), 'in such manner as the Legislature shall provide')
threshold.quote: If the majority of the electors voting with regard to said question at said election vote in the affirmative, said judge shall be retained in office for an additional term. If the majority of the voters voting on said question at said election vote in the negative, a vacancy in said office shall occur at the end of the term of office of said judge.

p.not_computed: fewer than 100 like measures in earlier years in the sources taken in (52) for the class 'statewide retention'
